meta.description: Allows bank operations staff to request and submit transaction reports (monthly, yearly, or custom date range) for the credit card portfolio by launching a batch reporting job directly from an online CICS screen.
meta.process_description: The program presents an online screen where an authorised user selects a report period type: Monthly (automatically covering the current calendar month), Yearly (automatically covering the full current calendar year), or Custom (where the user manually enters a start and end date). After validating the selected dates, the program constructs a complete JCL job stream — including the date range parameters — and submits it to the internal reader (an extra-partition Transient Data Queue), which causes the mainframe job scheduler to execute the batch transaction report program (TRANREPT procedure) asynchronously. The resulting report covers credit card transactions stored in the TRANSACT file for the specified period.

files.TRANSACT: The credit card transaction master file containing the transaction records that will be extracted and reported on by the submitted batch job

business_rules: Monthly report: date range is automatically set to the first day through the last day of the current calendar month — the user does not manually enter dates.
Yearly report: date range is automatically set to January 1st through December 31st of the current calendar year — the user does not manually enter dates.

Custom report: all six date fields (start month, start day, start year, end month, end day, end year) are mandatory — any missing field produces a specific field-level error message and halts submission.
Custom date fields must be numeric and within valid calendar ranges: month must be 01–12, day must be 01–31.
Date validation is performed using the CSUTLDTC utility (which calls CEEDAYS) to confirm that entered dates are real calendar dates before job submission.
The batch job is submitted via an extra-partition Transient Data Queue (internal reader), meaning the report runs asynchronously and does not block the online user session.
Navigation: PF3 returns the user to the main menu (COMEN01C); if the session is new (EIBCALEN=0), the user is redirected to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C).
Only one report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) may be selected per submission; the program evaluates them in priority order.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Top-level working storage group holding all operational variables used during the report request and job submission process.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this CICS program ('CORPT00C'), used for navigation, error logging, and communication area routing so the system knows which program is currently handling the report request screen.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier ('CR00') assigned to this report request screen. It is used to re-invoke the same screen after user input, maintaining session continuity between the operator's interactions with the report submission form.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The status or error message displayed at the bottom of the report request screen to inform the bank operations staff of validation failures (e.g., missing date fields) or successful job submission confirmation.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACT-FILE
variables.description: The logical name of the credit card transaction master file ('TRANSACT'). This identifies the data source that the submitted batch report job will read to extract and report on transaction activity for the selected date range.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An error indicator flag that controls whether the report request screen must be redisplayed with a validation error. When set to 'Y', it signals that the operator's input (e.g., custom date fields) failed validation and the job must not be submitted until corrections are made.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name indicating that a validation error has been detected in the report request (e.g., a missing or invalid custom date field), blocking job submission and requiring the screen to be redisplayed with an error message.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that no validation errors exist in the report request, meaning all required date fields are present and valid and the batch report job may proceed to submission.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACT-EOF
variables.description: An end-of-file indicator for the TRANSACT credit card transaction file. When set to 'Y', it signals that all transaction records have been read, controlling the loop that processes transaction data during any online file browsing or validation activity.

variables.name: TRANSACT-EOF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the end of the transaction master file has been reached and no more transaction records are available to be read or processed.

variables.name: TRANSACT-NOT-EOF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the transaction master file still has unread records remaining, allowing continued processing of transaction data.

variables.name: WS-SEND-ERASE-FLG
variables.description: A screen display control flag that determines whether the report request screen should be sent with a full erase (clearing all previous content) or as a partial update. An initial full erase ensures the operator sees a clean form when first entering the screen.

variables.name: SEND-ERASE-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating the report request screen should be fully erased and redrawn, typically used on first entry to present a clean report selection form to the operator.

variables.name: SEND-ERASE-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating the report request screen should be refreshed without a full erase, typically used when redisplaying the form after a validation error so that previously entered data is preserved.

variables.name: WS-END-LOOP
variables.description: A loop control flag used during JCL record writing or file processing. When set to 'Y', it signals that all required records (e.g., all JCL lines for the batch job) have been written and the loop should terminate.

variables.name: END-LOOP-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the processing loop (e.g., writing JCL records to the internal reader for batch job submission) has completed and should exit.

variables.name: END-LOOP-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the processing loop is still active and more records (e.g., additional JCL lines) remain to be written for the batch job submission.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after each CICS service call (e.g., writing to the internal reader, reading a file). A non-zero value indicates a system-level failure during report job submission or file access, which must be handled before proceeding.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code accompanying the response code, providing additional detail about why a CICS service call failed during report job submission or file operations, used for error diagnosis and handling.

variables.name: WS-REC-COUNT
variables.description: A counter tracking the number of records processed (e.g., JCL lines written to the internal reader during batch job submission), used to control iteration through the job stream template.

variables.name: WS-IDX
variables.description: A general-purpose index or counter used to iterate through the JCL job stream records when writing each 80-byte line to the internal reader for batch report job submission.

variables.name: WS-REPORT-NAME
variables.description: A human-readable label identifying the type of report the operator has requested — 'Monthly', 'Yearly', or 'Custom'. This value is displayed on the screen to confirm the report type selected before the batch job is submitted.

variables.name: WS-START-DATE
variables.description: The fully formatted start date of the reporting period in YYYY-MM-DD format. For Monthly and Yearly reports this is automatically calculated; for Custom reports it is assembled from the operator's individual field entries. This date defines the beginning of the transaction data range to be included in the batch report.

variables.name: WS-START-DATE-YYYY
variables.description: The four-digit year component of the report start date (e.g., '2024'). For Monthly/Yearly reports this is derived from the current system date; for Custom reports it is entered by the operator and validated before job submission.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A literal hyphen separator between the year and month components of the start date, ensuring the date is formatted as YYYY-MM-DD for correct parsing by the batch report program.

variables.name: WS-START-DATE-MM
variables.description: The two-digit month component of the report start date (01–12). For Monthly/Yearly reports this is set automatically; for Custom reports it is entered by the operator and must be a valid calendar month before the job is submitted.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A literal hyphen separator between the month and day components of the start date, maintaining the YYYY-MM-DD format required by the batch report program.

variables.name: WS-START-DATE-DD
variables.description: The two-digit day component of the report start date (01–31). For Monthly reports this is always '01' (first of the month); for Custom reports it is entered by the operator and validated as a real calendar date before job submission.

variables.name: WS-END-DATE
variables.description: The fully formatted end date of the reporting period in YYYY-MM-DD format. For Monthly reports this is the last day of the current month; for Yearly reports it is December 31st; for Custom reports it is assembled from the operator's entries. This date defines the upper boundary of transaction data included in the batch report.

variables.name: WS-END-DATE-YYYY
variables.description: The four-digit year component of the report end date (e.g., '2024'). Automatically set for Monthly and Yearly reports; entered by the operator for Custom reports and validated before the batch job is submitted.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A literal hyphen separator between the year and month components of the end date, ensuring the date is formatted as YYYY-MM-DD for correct parsing by the batch report program.

variables.name: WS-END-DATE-MM
variables.description: The two-digit month component of the report end date (01–12). For Monthly reports this is the current month; for Yearly reports this is '12' (December); for Custom reports it is entered by the operator and validated as a real calendar month.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A literal hyphen separator between the month and day components of the end date, maintaining the YYYY-MM-DD format required by the batch report program.

variables.name: WS-END-DATE-DD
variables.description: The two-digit day component of the report end date (01–31). For Monthly reports this is the last calendar day of the current month; for Yearly reports this is '31' (December 31st); for Custom reports it is entered by the operator and validated as a real calendar date.

variables.name: WS-DATE-FORMAT
variables.description: The date format mask ('YYYY-MM-DD') passed to the CSUTLDTC date validation utility (CEEDAYS) to confirm that the operator-entered custom dates represent real calendar dates before the batch report job is submitted.

variables.name: WS-NUM-99
variables.description: A general-purpose two-digit numeric work field used for intermediate calculations, such as determining the last day of the current month when automatically setting the end date for a Monthly report.

variables.name: WS-NUM-9999
variables.description: A general-purpose four-digit numeric work field used for intermediate calculations, such as handling year values when automatically computing date ranges for Monthly or Yearly reports.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-AMT
variables.description: A formatted display field for a credit card transaction amount, supporting values up to $99,999,999.99 with an explicit sign. Used to present individual transaction dollar amounts on screen during any online transaction review associated with the report process.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-DATE
variables.description: A formatted display field for a credit card transaction date in MM/DD/YY format, used to present the date of an individual transaction on screen during any online transaction review associated with the report process.

variables.name: JCL-RECORD
variables.description: A single 80-byte line of JCL (Job Control Language) that is written one record at a time to the CICS internal reader (Transient Data Queue) to submit the TRNRPT00 batch transaction report job. Each write of this field sends one JCL statement to the job scheduler.

variables.name: JOB-DATA
variables.description: The complete pre-built JCL job stream template for the TRNRPT00 batch transaction report job. This structure contains all the JCL statements needed to run the report, with placeholders for the start and end dates that are filled in at submission time based on the operator's report type selection.

variables.name: JOB-DATA-1
variables.description: The sequential collection of 80-byte JCL records that make up the batch report job stream, including job card statements, execution parameters, and date range parameters, written line by line to the internal reader to launch the TRNRPT00 report job.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: One of the fixed JCL statement lines (e.g., JOB card, EXEC statement, DD statements) that form the static, non-date-dependent portions of the TRNRPT00 batch report job stream submitted to the internal reader.

variables.name: FILLER-1
variables.description: The JCL parameter record line that carries the report start date into the batch job. It is composed of a fixed JCL keyword prefix, the dynamically inserted start date value, and a closing delimiter, forming the complete PARM start-date statement passed to the TRNRPT00 program.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The fixed JCL keyword prefix text (e.g., '// PARM.STEP=(''') that precedes the start date value in the batch job parameter record, providing the correct JCL syntax for passing the start date to the TRNRPT00 report program.

variables.name: PARM-START-DATE-1
variables.description: The start date of the reporting period (in YYYY-MM-DD format) injected into the JCL job stream as a parameter for the TRNRPT00 batch report program. This tells the batch job which date to begin extracting transactions from the TRANSACT file.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The closing delimiter and padding of the JCL start-date parameter record, providing the correct JCL syntax (closing quote and remaining spaces) to complete the 80-byte parameter statement line for the batch report job.

variables.name: FILLER-2
variables.description: The JCL parameter record line that carries the report end date into the batch job. It is composed of a fixed JCL keyword prefix, the dynamically inserted end date value, and a closing delimiter, forming the complete PARM end-date statement passed to the TRNRPT00 program.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The fixed JCL keyword prefix text that precedes the end date value in the batch job parameter record, providing the correct JCL syntax for passing the end date to the TRNRPT00 report program.

variables.name: PARM-END-DATE-1
variables.description: The end date of the reporting period (in YYYY-MM-DD format) injected into the JCL job stream as a parameter for the TRNRPT00 batch report program. This tells the batch job which date to stop extracting transactions from the TRANSACT file, defining the upper boundary of the report.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The closing delimiter and padding of the JCL end-date parameter record, providing the correct JCL syntax (closing quote and remaining spaces) to complete the 80-byte parameter statement line for the batch report job.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A fixed, pre-built line of JCL job stream text (80 bytes, the standard JCL record length) that forms part of the batch report job template. This represents one static line of the job definition — such as a JOB card, EXEC statement, or DD statement — that does not change between report submissions.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Another fixed, pre-built line of JCL job stream text forming part of the batch transaction report job template. Like its sibling above, this is a static JCL record (e.g., a SYSIN DD or output dataset definition) that is written unchanged to the internal reader every time a report is submitted.

variables.name: FILLER-3
variables.description: The dynamic JCL parameter record within the batch job stream that carries the reporting date range. This is the one line of the JCL template that changes per submission — it is populated at runtime with the start and end dates of the requested report period before the job is sent to the internal reader.

variables.name: PARM-START-DATE-2
variables.description: The start date of the reporting period (in YYYY-MM-DD format) injected into the JCL PARM statement as the second occurrence of the start date parameter. This value tells the batch transaction report program (TRNRPT00) where to begin extracting transactions — e.g., the first day of the selected month, year, or custom range. It is written directly into the job stream record submitted to the internal reader.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A single blank character used as a delimiter between the start date and end date parameters within the JCL PARM record. This separator ensures the batch program can correctly parse the two date values passed on the parameter line.

variables.name: PARM-END-DATE-2
variables.description: The end date of the reporting period (in YYYY-MM-DD format) injected into the JCL PARM statement as the second occurrence of the end date parameter. This value tells the batch transaction report program (TRNRPT00) where to stop extracting transactions — e.g., the last day of the selected month, year, or custom range. Together with PARM-START-DATE-2, it defines the complete date window for the report.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding spaces that fill the remainder of the 80-byte JCL parameter record after the start and end dates have been placed. JCL records must be exactly 80 bytes; this filler ensures the dynamic parameter line conforms to that fixed-length requirement when written to the internal reader.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Another static JCL record in the pre-built batch job template, representing a fixed line of the job stream (such as a DD statement for the transaction input file TRANSACT or a report output dataset) that is written unchanged to the internal reader during job submission.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: The final static JCL record in the pre-built batch job template, representing the last fixed line of the job stream (such as a null DD statement or job terminator) that closes out the JCL submitted to the internal reader for the transaction report batch job.

variables.name: JOB-DATA-2
variables.description: An alternative view of the complete JCL job stream template (JOB-DATA-1) that breaks it into an array of individual 80-byte lines. This redefinition allows the program to loop through the job stream record by record and write each line sequentially to the internal reader (Transient Data Queue), which is how batch jobs are submitted from an online CICS screen.

variables.name: JOB-LINES
variables.description: A single 80-byte JCL record within the batch job stream, accessed by index when writing the job to the internal reader. Each occurrence represents one line of the JCL submitted for the TRNRPT00 transaction report job — the program iterates through these lines to submit the complete job to the batch queue, one record at a time.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-PARM
variables.description: The parameter block passed to the CSUTLDTC date validation utility (which internally calls the IBM Language Environment CEEDAYS service). Before submitting a custom date range report, the program uses this structure to verify that the user-entered start and end dates are real calendar dates — preventing invalid dates like February 30th from being passed to the batch job.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-DATE
variables.description: The specific date value (in YYYY-MM-DD format) being submitted to the date validation utility for verification. The program loads either the custom start date or end date here before calling CSUTLDTC to confirm it is a valid calendar date prior to job submission.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT
variables.description: Specifies the format of the date being validated (e.g., 'YYYY-MM-DD') so the CSUTLDTC utility knows how to interpret the date string. This ensures the validation service correctly parses the year, month, and day components of the user-entered custom report date.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-RESULT
variables.description: The result block returned by the CSUTLDTC date validation utility after checking whether the submitted date is a valid calendar date. The program inspects this structure to determine whether to proceed with job submission or display a date validation error to the operations staff member.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD
variables.description: The severity code returned by the date validation utility indicating whether the date check passed or failed. A non-zero or error severity code signals that the user-entered custom report date is invalid (e.g., a non-existent date), causing the program to set the error flag and redisplay the screen with an appropriate message instead of submitting the batch job.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Reserved/unused bytes within the date validation result structure returned by CSUTLDTC. These bytes are part of the utility's fixed return area layout but carry no business meaning for this program.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM
variables.description: The message number returned by the date validation utility identifying the specific type of validation result or error. This code can be used to distinguish between different failure reasons (e.g., invalid month, invalid day) when the entered custom report date fails validation.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG
variables.description: The human-readable error message returned by the date validation utility when a custom report date fails validation. This message describes why the date is invalid and may be surfaced to the operations staff member on the report request screen to guide them in correcting their date entry.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area passed between online program invocations, used to maintain session state across screen interactions. For this report request program, it carries context such as the logged-in user's identity and program navigation information, enabling the system to know whether the user is entering the screen for the first time or returning after a validation error.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: The linkage section representation of the CICS communication area data passed into this program. Even though it is defined as a single byte here, it serves as the anchor point for the CARDDEMO-COMMAREA structure (from COCOM01Y) which is overlaid on top of it, providing access to the user ID, navigation context, and session state needed to process the report request screen correctly.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central control paragraph that governs the entire lifecycle of the report request screen session: it determines whether the user is new or returning, routes them to the correct screen or action based on their input, and ensures the session remains active after each interaction.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the user's report submission request by determining the selected report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), calculating or validating the appropriate date range, and triggering the batch transaction report job. It enforces all business rules around date completeness, numeric validity, and calendar correctness before allowing the job to be submitted.

paragraphs.name: SUBMIT-JOB-TO-INTRDR
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the final confirmation step before submitting the batch transaction report job to the mainframe scheduler. It validates the operator's explicit yes/no confirmation, then sequentially writes each line of the pre-built JCL job stream to the internal reader queue, which triggers asynchronous execution of the batch report.

paragraphs.name: WIRTE-JOBSUB-TDQ
paragraphs.description: This paragraph physically submits one line of the constructed batch job to the mainframe internal reader queue, which triggers asynchronous execution of the transaction report. If the submission fails, it raises an error and returns the user to the report request screen with an appropriate message.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Transfers control back to the previous screen in the CardDemo application, ensuring the user is returned to an appropriate destination — defaulting to the sign-on screen if no prior navigation context exists. This supports the PF3 back-navigation business rule, maintaining a coherent user session flow.

paragraphs.name: SEND-TRNRPT-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Renders the transaction report request screen to the bank operations user, displaying any validation messages or status information. It determines whether to fully refresh the screen or perform a lighter update, then hands control back to CICS to await the next user interaction.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-CICS
paragraphs.description: Suspends the current online session and returns control to CICS, keeping the report request screen active and ready to receive the next user interaction. The session context and any in-progress data are preserved so the screen can be redisplayed seamlessly when the user next interacts with it.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-TRNRPT-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Captures the report request submitted by the bank operations staff member from the online transaction report screen, reading all field entries (report type selection and any custom date inputs) into memory for subsequent validation and processing.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Populates the standard screen header area with current date, time, application titles, transaction identity, and program identity before displaying the report request screen to the user. This ensures every screen presented to bank operations staff carries consistent, accurate contextual information for audit and navigation purposes.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS
paragraphs.description: Resets the report request screen to a clean state before presenting it to the user, clearing all previously entered or displayed values so that no stale data from a prior session or submission influences the new request.
